subject: maths
title: Time and Measurement - Days, Length and Mass

steps.title: Measure fairly

options.label: How many same-size cubes cover the pencil with no gaps?
On a balance, B goes down and A goes up. Which object is heavier?

steps.hint: Count each cube once. Gaps would leave part of the length unmeasured.
steps.explanation: Use equal touching cubes, the day sequence and a balance.
steps.shortExplanation: Make, count or compare the objects. Explain what changed.

mathWorkshop.title: Measure fairly
mathWorkshop.goal: Use equal touching cubes, the day sequence and a balance.

tasks.prompt: How many same-size cubes cover the pencil with no gaps?
tasks.feedback: Six equal cubes cover the whole pencil length without gaps.
tasks.hint: Count each cube once. Gaps would leave part of the length unmeasured.

tasks.feedback: Tuesday comes after Monday in the repeating week.
tasks.hint: Find Monday in the day row, then read the next day.

tasks.prompt: On a balance, B goes down and A goes up. Which object is heavier?
tasks.feedback: The heavier side goes down, so object B is heavier.
tasks.hint: Look for the side that went down. Size alone cannot tell us mass.

parentReview.en: Guided practice is ungraded. Completion records the child doing the activities, not a book-question score.

steps.title: Maths discovery 2
steps.prompt: How many days are in a week?
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: There are 7 days before the week repeats.
steps.shortExplanation: There are 7 days before the week repeats.

steps.title: Maths discovery 3
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: Tuesday follows Monday. Thursday comes before Friday.
steps.shortExplanation: Tuesday follows Monday. Thursday comes before Friday.

steps.title: Maths discovery 4
steps.prompt: How many months are in a year?
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: A year has 12 months, from January to December.
steps.shortExplanation: A year has 12 months, from January to December.

steps.title: Maths discovery 5
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: February is the month after January.
steps.shortExplanation: February is the month after January.

steps.title: Maths discovery 6
steps.prompt: How many cubes long is the pencil?
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: Six equal cubes cover the pencil length with no gaps.
steps.shortExplanation: Six equal cubes cover the pencil length with no gaps.

steps.title: Maths discovery 7
steps.prompt: On this balance, B is down and A is up. Which is heavier?
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: The heavier side goes down, so B is heavier.
steps.shortExplanation: The heavier side goes down, so B is heavier.

steps.title: Maths discovery 8
steps.prompt: A bigger object is always heavier.
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: A large pillow can be lighter than a small stone.
steps.shortExplanation: A large pillow can be lighter than a small stone.

source.answerKeyText: False. A big pillow is lighter than a small stone.

steps.title: Maths discovery 9
steps.prompt: Put these in order, heaviest first.
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: A typical chair is heavier than a book, and a feather is lightest.
steps.shortExplanation: A typical chair is heavier than a book, and a feather is lightest.

steps.title: Maths discovery 10
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: 12 months is the answer. The months run from January through December.
steps.shortExplanation: 12 months is the answer. The months run from January through December.

steps.title: Maths discovery 11
steps.prompt: On a balance, the heavier side goes...
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: Down is the answer. More mass makes that side lower.
steps.shortExplanation: Down is the answer. More mass makes that side lower.

steps.title: Maths discovery 12
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: No gaps is the answer. Touching units cover the whole length.
steps.shortExplanation: No gaps is the answer. Touching units cover the whole length.

steps.title: Maths discovery 13
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: Sunday is the answer. The week cycles back to Sunday.
steps.shortExplanation: Sunday is the answer. The week cycles back to Sunday.

steps.title: Maths discovery 14
steps.hint: Check the day order; use equal units or see which side goes down.
steps.explanation: A watermelon is the answer. A typical watermelon has more mass than a grape or strawberry.
steps.shortExplanation: A watermelon is the answer. A typical watermelon has more mass than a grape or strawberry.

stickers.meaning: How heavy or light an object is.

homeActivities.text: With an adult, measure a spoon using equal-size bricks with no gaps. Compare mass with a safe balance and talk about days and months.
homeActivities.textAr: مع حد كبير، قيسوا معلقة بمكعبات نفس الحجم من غير فراغات بينها. قارنوا التقل بميزان آمن، واتكلموا عن أيام الأسبوع وشهور السنة.
homeActivities.safety: An adult supervises. Keep small objects away from younger children. An adult handles scissors. Use water at the sink, away from electrical items.
homeActivities.safetyAr: لازم شخص كبير يكون موجود. خلّي الحاجات الصغيرة بعيد عن الأطفال الأصغر، والكبير يمسك المقص. أنشطة المية تكون عند الحوض وبعيد عن الكهرباء.
